cd /tmp/arena-ws.1UR284 && cat > Q-REPORT.md <<'EOF'
# Quarterly operations report — May–July 2026

## Summary

The quarter delivered €1,233,225 in revenue against €467,940 in costs, leaving
a net of €765,285 and a margin of 62.1%. In aggregate that is a strong result,
but the shape of the quarter matters more than the total: performance peaked in
June and deteriorated through July.

Revenue grew 4.6% in June, then fell 9.6% in July — ending the quarter not just
below June but 5.5% below where May started. Costs moved the other way, rising
€7,420 from May to June and then holding flat, so the July revenue drop landed
almost entirely on the bottom line. Monthly margin tracked accordingly: 63.4%
in May, 63.2% in June, 59.4% in July. The quarterly margin of 62.1% is
therefore a flattering average of a declining trend rather than a stable run
rate.

The customer picture shows the same deceleration, and it is the more concerning
of the two. We added 153 net customers across the quarter, but the monthly
contribution halved and halved again: 69 in May, 52 in June, 32 in July. Both
sides of the equation moved against us — new signings fell each month (86, 74,
63) while churn rose sharply (17, 22, 31). Churn as a share of new signings
went from roughly one in five in May to nearly one in two in July. Support was
the bright spot: the close rate improved every month (92.1%, 97.0%, 97.7%) to
finish the quarter at 95.5%, with July's lower ticket volume handled well.

## Key figures

| Metric | Value |
|---|---|
| Quarterly revenue | €1,233,225 |
| Quarterly costs | €467,940 |
| Net | €765,285 |
| Margin | 62.1% |
| Net customer adds | 153 |
| Ticket close rate | 95.5% |
| June revenue growth | 4.6% |
| July revenue growth | -9.6% |

## Notes

- **Data discrepancy in the June monthly.** June's stated total costs
  (€158,240) do not match the sum of its own cost lines (€158,540) — a €300
  gap. This report uses the line-item sum, on the assumption the stated total
  is a transcription slip. The effect is immaterial (quarterly margin rounds to
  62.1% either way), but the June monthly should be corrected at source.
- **Churn is the headline risk.** Churn nearly doubled over the quarter (17 to
  31) while signings fell. If the July rate persists, net adds turn negative
  within a month or two even with signings flat. This deserves a root-cause
  review rather than being read as normal variance.
- **Marketing spend was cut in the month revenue fell.** Marketing dropped from
  €21,400 in June to €16,980 in July (-20.7%), coinciding with the -9.6%
  revenue month and the weakest signings of the quarter. The monthlies do not
  say which drove which; worth establishing before setting the Q4 budget.
- **Costs are now structurally flat, not flexible.** Payroll was identical in
  June and July (€98,100) and cloud rose every month (€21,310 to €24,760).
  With roughly two-thirds of the cost base fixed, further revenue softness
  passes straight through to margin.
- **Office & travel grew 33% over the quarter** (€9,240 to €12,310) with no
  explanation in the monthlies — small in absolute terms, but the fastest-
  growing line proportionally.
EOF
echo "--- written ---" && wc -l Q-REPORT.md && git status --short
echo "=== headings ===" && grep -n '^##' Q-REPORT.md && echo "=== row labels ===" && sed -n '/^| Metric/,/July revenue growth/p' Q-REPORT.md | awk -F'|' 'NR>2{print NR-2": ["$2"]"}'

`Q-REPORT.md` is written — three headings in order, all eight row labels exact, no commits made.

**Quarter at a glance:** €1,233,225 revenue, €467,940 costs, €765,285 net, 62.1% margin, 153 net adds, 95.5% close rate, +4.6% June, **-9.6% July**.

Two things worth your attention:

**A data discrepancy in the June monthly.** June's stated total costs (€158,240) don't match the sum of its own cost lines (€158,540) — a €300 gap. May and July both reconcile exactly, so June is the outlier. I used the line-item sum on the assumption the total is a transcription slip, and flagged it in Notes for correction at source. The choice is immaterial to the report: quarterly margin rounds to 62.1% either way.

**The quarterly totals flatter a declining trend.** The 62.1% margin is an average of 63.4% / 63.2% / 59.4%, and the 153 net adds are 69 / 52 / 32 — halving each month, with signings falling *and* churn nearly doubling (17 → 31) simultaneously. I wrote the Summary to lead with the trajectory rather than the aggregate, since a leadership reader who sees only the totals would take away the wrong picture. Notes also flags that marketing was cut 20.7% in the same month revenue fell 9.6% — the monthlies don't establish causality, but it's the obvious question before the next budget is set.
